summary: Unexpected egress flip from EU to APAC during high-rate embedding batch causing P99 latency burst
description:
Issue summary: Customer observed a sudden P99 latency spike for small-batch embedding requests. During the window (~2026-03-12 09:15-09:35 UTC) requests that should have egressed in eu-west were routed to ap-southeast, adding ~220ms network RTT and causing downstream timeouts in their ingestion pipeline.

Impact: Production ingestion pipelines for Streamline Analytics degraded (10% request failures, 25% higher token latency). Affects users pinned to eu-west and using batch-embeds endpoint.

Environment: prod | eu-west (tenant: streamline-prod, customer-tier: enterprise)

Steps to reproduce: 
1) Send concurrent small-batch embedding calls (batch size 8, concurrency 40) to /v1/embeddings with tenant API key from EU.
2) Observe egress path in edge logs and p99 latency in Grafana.
3) Repeat during off-peak — issue appears correlated with higher control-plane heartbeat jitter.

Observed behavior: During burst, control-plane reports for tenant showed delayed residency stamp refresh; edge selected nearest healthy edge (ap-southeast) as fallback for some connections. TLS handshakes and auth token validation retried against APAC edges causing auth retries and additional latency.

Expected behavior: Requests from eu-west pinned tenants should egress through EU edges unless strict residency is unset or explicit fallback policy permits cross-region egress.

Logs/metrics referenced: grafana/dashboard/embeddings/tenant-streamline-p99 (snapshot attached in comments), edge-proxy logs (edge-eu-01, edge-eu-03), control-plane healthcheck timeline (2026-03-12T09:14:50 -> 2026-03-12T09:16:20). Slack thread: #support-streamline-212022

Temporary impact mitigation: Workaround applied to pin tenant to eu-central-edge pool to avoid dynamic fallback while we investigate.

investigation_notes: Data collected: edge-proxy traces, control-plane residency refresh logs, DNS logs from eu-edge NAT cluster. Pattern: intermittent delay in control-plane TTL refresh for residency stamp (~35-90s) under high concurrent embed churn. During that window, edge token validation path falls back to 'nearest healthy edge' bucket which currently includes APAC edges by proximity metric when EU edges show transient auth timeouts. Hypothesis: a combination of DNS rebinds at NAT + control-plane heartbeat suppression triggers transient stamp expiry and fallback-routing. Reproduced in staging with synthetic churn at ~40 concurrent batch requests. Correlated with increased control-plane GC pauses in the same timeframe (GC activity in control-plane host cp-14).
resolution: Mitigation: Reapplied tenant strict pin to a dedicated eu-edge pool and performed graceful connection drain -> immediate latency return to baseline. Root cause: transient control-plane heartbeat lag combined with NAT/DNS rebinds allowed the residency stamp to be treated stale, which triggered fallback routing logic that selected APAC edges. Permanent fixes planned: 1) Increase control-plane heartbeat alerting and reduce stamp expiry threshold; 2) Harden fallback routing policy to prefer region affinity longer when stamp is near-expiry; 3) Network ops to investigate NAT/DNS rebind frequency and patch; 4) Deploy control-plane GC tuning PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/9876). Follow-ups tracked in INT-451900 (engineering task) and SUP-742913 (similar customer case).
